name: Adresse N-Ways Côte d'Ivoire

officialFirst.text: Where the State has already given a gate an address, that address is the address and comes first.
officialFirst.meaning: Where an official door-level address exists, N-Ways shows it first, exactly as officially written, and puts no N-Ways plate on that gate. The compound keeps its N-Ways code beside the official address (said on the phone, and telling apart the households of a cour behind one gate), with the navigation aids (gate position, building profile, Plus Code). P.O. boxes and office codes are pointers, not addresses.

coverage.data: street list with ID_VOIE public (MCLU PDF, Sep 2025); address points on the PADA partner geoportal under the 24 Jan 2023 data-sharing convention, not open: access requested
coverage.nways: import and show PADA exactly; gate pin, profile, Plus Code; no N-Ways number or plate; registry key PADA:<ID_VOIE>:<number>

coverage.area: Abidjan precarious quarters (excluded by PADA, ~20% of residents)
Abidjan gates PADA did not number (back compounds, new builds)
coverage.nways: N-Ways code marked 'hors PADA'; alias if PADA numbers it later
N-Ways codes in the app, no plates until PAVI delivers; then the official address is shown first and the N-Ways code stays beside it

coverage.official: PADA numeric code d'adresse (approved Feb 2025): five digits, département (3) + commune (2), written after the street
coverage.data: format public; no open table of codes

designCriteria: 1. Easy to remember and zero effort to get: a short plate name of a place people already use (at most 12 characters and 2 words) + a 4-digit number (5 for 311 names) read as two pairs. 'Name NNNN' is unique in the whole country on its own.
2. Beside official systems: PADA street address shown first in Abidjan; never a 'postal code'; never shaped like PADA's numeric code d'adresse.
3. The compound (cour, concession, parcelle) is the address; the gate is where the driver goes.
4. Stable: a number is never moved or reused; renames change aliases only.
5. Works offline; open method and data; codes describe places, never people.

rules: the name is the area's plate name: at most 12 characters and 2 words (plateNames)
digits only after a place name
unique nationally on its own: never needs the commune or town after it
4 digits, or 5 for names whose national range needs them; the length is fixed per name
read in pairs like phone numbers

written.label: the commune in brackets is a display label only; it is never needed to decode, and a label that contradicts the decoded area makes the code invalid

plate.pada: No N-Ways plate on any gate PADA numbered: the State's plate is the plate. Plates only where no official address exists; none in PAVI towns before PAVI delivers (codes in the app there).

spoken.note: Area names are said as locals say them (Baoulé, Dioula, Ébrié, Bété... place names); digits in French pairs, as Ivorian 10-digit phone numbers are read.

official.pattern: <number>, <official street name>, <commune> exactly as PADA writes it
official.example: 115, Rue des Moineaux, Le Plateau (illustrative number)

units.level: sous-préfecture (509 official; 510 polygons in the CNTIG/OCHA 2018 layer) + the 10 historical communes of Abidjan (inside the Abidjan sous-préfecture)
units.code: 6 digits. Sous-préfecture: digits of the OCHA/CNTIG pcode (CI010101 -> 010101 = district 01, département 01, SP 01). Abidjan communes: interim 010111-010120 (alphabetical: Abobo 010111 ... Yopougon 010120).
units.why: PADA's code d'adresse is 'based on the codification of geographic circonscriptions ... identifiers of the Département and the Commune/Sous-Préfecture' (KOACI, 27 Feb 2025). Using the same level makes a 1:1 mapping table possible the day the official codes are published. Interim codes are replaced by a published alias table, never by changing issued codes.

codeAreas.what: A frozen polygon named after the quartier, village or campement people use, inside one unit. Its numbers come from its frozen block in the national range of its name, so a number is unique for that name in the whole country.
codeAreas.interim: Nearest named OSM place (city, town, village, hamlet, suburb, quarter, neighbourhood, locality) inside the same unit; 9,834 areas in model/areas/areas.csv. The 'Abidjan' city node is excluded inside the communes.
codeAreas.frozenAt: first issue of a code in the area; boundaries then change only for unissued land
codeAreas.index: 3 digits, rank inside the unit north to south then west to east at freezing; stored, never recomputed
codeAreas.split: An area with compounds x 2 > 9,000 is split by quartier names (PADA quartier column, OSM, people) before any code is issued in it; where no names exist it keeps one large block in a 5-digit range and is flagged for splitting.

evidence.method: 10% building sample (OSM + Google/Microsoft footprints) assigned to nearest named place; compounds = structures x 0.834 (Abidjan ratio). tools/national_areas.py, model/stats/national-areas.json.

number.digits: 4, or 5 for names whose national range needs them; fixed per name
number.capacityRule: per area: block = max(100, 2 x compounds rounded up to 100) inside its name's national range (nationalNames)
number.order: Hilbert curve, order 16, over the area's frozen frame (bounding box), on the compound's reference point (gate if known, else area-weighted centroid of its structures)
number.step: s = floor(blockSize / (N x 1.5)), at least 1; compound i gets blockLo + i x s
number.infill: new compound: free number between the numbers of its Hilbert neighbours, closest to the midpoint; else the lowest free number of the block's tail reserve; else a new block from the name's spare
number.uniqueness: a number is unique for its name in the whole country

check.over: name key as digits (a-z -> 10-35, 0-9 -> 00-09) + number; the area is bound by the frozen block table (the number decides the area; the machine form's unit+area must own the number's block)
detects: every swap of two adjacent digits
check.where: written form, machine form, plates, forms, partner APIs; optional when a remembered code is typed (it then decodes to one area, shown before guiding)
check.why: hashing the area digits in would let a number typo that moves to another block change several input digits at once, which Damm does not guarantee to catch; binding by block keeps the guarantee

spot.system: Open Location Code (Plus Codes), implemented in engine/reference/ci_engine.py
spot.cell: 1/40000 deg x 1/32000 deg, about 2.8 m x 3.5 m
spot.short: OLC short code against the reference town of the unit: 'PWPQ+2J2 Bouaké' (= 6CVPPWPQ+2J2) (references in model/areas/references.csv)
spot.why: Open and free, offline, already printed by common map apps; La Poste CI promotes proprietary what3words - N-Ways offers the open alternative and never depends on w3w. Spots are shared as links (nways.ng/p/<code>), not memorised.
spot.regionsFile: model/regions.json shows 3 m spot codes would need 7-8 characters per district; OLC's 11 characters cover the country with no tables.

compound.unit: plot / compound (cour, concession, parcelle, villa with its fence, immeuble with its plot)

detection.source: closed OSM barrier=wall|fence|hedge ways; N-Ways compounds.geojsonseq (kind estate|government|military|police)

detection.what: structure < 25 m2 joins the nearest structure >= 25 m2 whose footprint is within 5 m

detection.source: SIGFU / IDUFCI / ACD parcel where the compound's owner or a partner provides it

detection.what: 'these buildings are one home', 'this is the gate', from residents, visitors and couriers; settled by agreement
anything else is its own compound

compound.estates: an enclosure > 6,000 m2 holding many compounds (cité SICOGI/SOGEFIHA, gated lotissement) is an ESTATE: it gets its gate(s) as entrances of type estate-gate; compounds inside keep their own codes; routing ends at the estate gate when the inside is private
compound.regroupingNeverChangesCodes: If later evidence merges two compounds, the older code survives and the other becomes an alias; if it splits one, the largest part keeps the code and the others get new numbers.

profile.useClass: residential-one-household | residential-multi-household (cour commune) | residential-multi-storey (immeuble) | mixed | commercial | institutional | industrial | agricultural (campement) | under-construction | unknown
profile.plotAreaM2: from enclosure, cadastral parcel or Add-my-home outline; else null
profile.households: number declared by the resident in Add my home; kept by the N-Ways app, never in the registry
profile.pada: list of {idVoie, street, number} on its gates
profile.parcelRefs: IDUFCI / ACD / lotissement îlot+lot, only with the owner's consent; never in the registry

structure.code: <compound machine form>.<n>, n = 1 for the largest footprint, then by size at freezing; new structures get the next n

residential: maison en bande / logement de cité (SICOGI, SOGEFIHA)
maison de village (villages Ébrié, villages ruraux)

profile.useConfidence: 0-1; evidence: OSM building tag 0.85, OSM shop/amenity tag on the footprint 0.75, N-Ways place inside the footprint 0.65, OSM landuse 0.5, size prior 0.3-0.4, default residential 0.45/0.55; +0.05 per agreeing source; residential + commercial evidence = mixed 0.6; a confirmed door/owner statement 0.9
profile.heightM: OSM height, else ML parquet h (Google/Microsoft), else null
profile.floors: OSM building:levels, else max(1, round((h - 1.5) / 3)), else 1
profile.name: businesses and public buildings only, as the business, the institution or the public record gives it
profile.sources: per attribute: {source, value, observedAt, confirmedAt}; sources: osm, google-open-buildings, microsoft, nways-places, nways-people, partner, pada, resident

kinds: door (porte de boutique dans le mur, entrée secondaire)
entrances.routing: the driver is taken to the primary gate, never to a footprint centroid

steps: stand at the gate: GPS averaged 5-10 s + one gate photo

outline the plot: tap corners on imagery | walk the inside of the wall with AR world tracking (ARKit/ARCore), anchored by GPS averaged over the walk, checked against imagery and footprints | import a géomètre plan / SIGFU-IDUFCI parcel (beacon coordinates typed or photographed; datum stated: ITRF2014@2010.0 per Décret 2019-220, or legacy Abidjan 1987 / Clarke 1880 converted)
describe it: households (private), structures, floors, use
get a PROVISIONAL code at once: next reserved number of the area (infill rule)
CONFIRMED by deliveries/arrivals at the gate, no neighbour dispute, or new imagery/footprints
checks: gate lies on or within 3 m of the outline
GPS vs AR outline agreement within 5 m
no overlap > 10% with an existing compound or parcel (overlap -> flagged, not issued)
addMyHome.offline: spot code (Plus Code) shown at once; compound code reserved from the downloaded area pack, confirmed on next connection
addMyHome.legal: An N-Ways code is an address, not a land title, an ACD, a certificat foncier or a plan. Only a géomètre-expert agréé plan approved by the MCLU (urban) or an AFOR certificat foncier (rural) has legal value. The flow says so before the code is shown.
addMyHome.privacy: kept: outline and gate photo; never: names, ID numbers, NNI, documents

gettingYourCode.appSavedHome: 0 steps to see ('Votre adresse N-Ways' card on the home screen), 1 tap to share (WhatsApp/SMS link nways.ng/a/<code>)
gettingYourCode.atTheGate: open the app -> 'Mon adresse ici' (1 tap) -> confirm 'this is my gate' (1 tap)
gettingYourCode.noSmartphone: plate or sticker on the gate; a relative, courier or partner looks it up for them
gettingYourCode.partners: API lookup by phone-free inputs: point, PADA address, area + number
notOffered: SMS lookup service (possible later option, not planned)

interop.pada: PADA is the address where it exists: entrance.pada {idVoie, street, number} imported from the MCLU street list and the PADA partner geoportal (access requested under the 2023 convention); until access, entered by people (plate photo / typed) and validated against the street list, never guessed; synced by ID_VOIE on each release; mismatches reported to the MCLU, not corrected by N-Ways
interop.padaCodeAdresse: mapping table unit -> official département + commune/SP code when published
interop.laPoste: B.P. text only for businesses that publish it; POLI couriers as partners
interop.parcels: IDUFCI / ACD / AFOR certificat foncier optional cross-references (private by default)
interop.plusCodes: every compound and gate also has its Plus Code

privacy.law: Loi n° 2013-450 du 19 juin 2013; authority ARTCI
obligations: prior authorisation for phone-number processing and for any transfer abroad (art. 7, art. 26); silence = refusal
published: names of businesses and public buildings
never: linking to the MaPoste NNI-linked box
privacy.precariousQuarters: codes are addresses, not rights or eviction lists: the registry is the same in every quarter and holds nothing about people; requests about people are answered only under a legal order, logged and reported

partners: District Autonome d'Abidjan and the 13 communes
La Poste de Côte d'Ivoire (incl. POLI)
governance.handOver: the repo can move to a national body if Côte d'Ivoire adopts the model

nationalNames.why: A code read on the phone or written on a parcel often travels without its commune, and place names repeat across the country: the remembered code must be unique nationally on its own; context (the app's position, a commune after a comma) is not allowed to decide.
nationalNames.replaces: the alternative where same-named areas were told apart by the commune ('Sicogi 48 17, Yopougon') and parsing could return several candidates

nameKey.function: engine/reference/ci_engine.py name_key, applied to the plate name; engine/SPEC.md 4.1
steps: first of several OSM names (A;B -> A)
NFKD, accents removed, lower case; oe/ae ligatures opened
words split on anything but a-z 0-9 (hyphens, apostrophes, dots, brackets, spaces)
drop le la les l de du des d et au aux
st->saint, ste->sainte, pk/kilometre->km, qt/qrt/qtier->quartier, Roman I-X -> digits
per word: final -s dropped (4+ letters); ou before a vowel -> w; y -> i; ph -> f; qu/q -> k; c before a/o/u -> k; doubled letters single
nameKey.languages: French plus the spellings of Akan (Baoulé, Agni), Mandé (Dioula, Malinké), Krou and Gur place names

range.fiveDigits: 10000-99999 if blocks + spare <= 90,000; 1000-9999 then never issued for that name
range.skippedStretches: a name never uses the five-digit numbers d0000-d9999 when the same name followed by the digit d is also a name ('Koffikro' and 'Koffikro 1'), so 'Koffikro 1 12 00' reads one way only

blocks.size: max(100, 2 x compounds today rounded up to 100): infill gaps + tail reserve inside each block
blocks.order: unit code, then area index; laid end to end from the bottom of the range

nationalNames.growth: new area with an existing name, or an area whose block is full: next block from the name's spare (above every existing block); a 4-digit name whose 4-digit space is used up continues in its 5-digit space; earlier codes never change
nationalNames.frozen: a block never moves, shrinks or is renumbered once a code is issued from it; renaming an area adds an alias and keeps its blocks

qualifier.when: a name whose blocks + spare exceed 90,000
qualifier.rule: each of its areas puts its unit (commune of Abidjan or sous-préfecture) in front, as people already say 'Yopougon Sicogi', 'Koumassi Remblais'; decided once per name, before its first issue, and listed

nationalNames.decode: name_key(typed name) -> the plate key (directly, or through the official-name alias table) + number -> the one block containing the number -> one area, or 'not issued'. Never more than one candidate.

largestSharedRange.name: Belleville
largestSharedRange.note: 10000-29999 skipped: Belleville 1 and Belleville 2 are names too; blocks 30000-82399

nationalNames.method: compounds per area from the 10% building sample (out/ci/sample.csv, 964,816 points) given to the nearest area point, x 10 x 0.834; recomputed with full footprints and frozen polygons before first issue

plateNames.why: Names taken as they are from map data are often too long to say; each code area has a plate name of at most 12 characters and 2 words.

limit.charsCount: every character of the NFC form: letters (an accented letter is one), spaces, hyphens, apostrophes
limit.wordsCount: parts between spaces or hyphens; linking words (de, du, des, d', la, le, les, l', et, sur, en, au, aux, à) do not count
limit.numberWords: one word holding digits allowed ("Riviéra 2", "Zone 4", "PK 18"), counted as a word and in the characters

fields.name: official / full area name (areas.csv name): small print on cards and plates, never required
fields.plate: plate name used in the code
fields.plateRule: as-is | cleaned | abbreviated | known | distinctive | council
fields.needsCouncilChoice: 1 when the commune (or sous-préfecture) must choose before first issue
fields.plateCandidates: up to 3, the first used provisionally
fields.plateSource: source of a known short form

derivation: known: documented short form people already say, with a source
clean: drop text in brackets or after a slash, generic words (Quartier, Cité, Lotissement, Zone, Secteur, Village de, Campement, Résidence(s)), linking words left at the ends
as-is or cleaned if it fits
abbreviated: Saint -> St, Sainte -> Ste (the name key expands them back)
distinctive: the rarest one or two whole words, preferring the end of the name; never cut inside a word

Ivorian check: an automatic short form may drop only generic or settlement words (Cité, Carrefour, Camp, Gare...) or the commune/sous-préfecture put in front of a quartier; any other word sends the area to the commune
council: everything else, with up to 3 candidates; a hyphenated village name over the limit offers its parts
plateNames.avoid: a short form equal to a sous-préfecture seat, a département, an Abidjan commune or a large city of the region (Yamoussoukro, Bamako, Ouagadougou, Accra...) is not taken automatically: a plate reading like another city would mislead; the area's own unit is allowed

aliases.rule: the official name typed instead of the plate name decodes, but only to the areas that carry that official name; an alias claimed by two plate names, or equal to another area's plate name, is dropped

known.source: fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocody ("2 Plateaux" in the sub-commune list); business addresses "Cocody II Plateaux", e.g. annuaireci.com/en/entreprises/cabinet-de-pediatrie-des-ii-plateaux-abidjan-cote-divoire/

plateNames.collisionAfterShortening: Cité Sicogi (Cocody) and Sicogi (Yopougon) are both "Sicogi": one national range, Sicogi · 1 05 00 is Cocody, Sicogi · 1 88 17 is Yopougon
plateNames.communeChoice: the commune or sous-préfecture confirms every flagged plate name; codes carry the first candidate until then, and a later choice is added as an alias without changing any number
